body.p: JALv3 stores arrays of BIT natively: one bit per element, packed without padding. A BIT array of N elements occupies (N+7)/8 bytes of data memory.
Elements are accessed with the ordinary subscript syntax, using either a constant or a runtime index. A BIT value can be tested directly or converted to a byte value:
body.codeblock: flags[0] = TRUE flags[idx] = FALSE VAR BYTE as_byte = BYTE(flags[0]) IF !flags[idx] THEN flags[1] = FALSE END IF IF flags[0] & flags[2] THEN flags[3] = TRUE END IF
body.p: Bit arrays may be passed to procedures as fixed-size or open-array formals. An IN OUT formal writes changes back to the caller's array:
body.codeblock: PROCEDURE read_fixed(BIT IN bits[4]) IS ... END PROCEDURE PROCEDURE read_open(BIT IN bits[]) IS ... END PROCEDURE PROCEDURE update(BIT IN OUT bits[17]) IS ... END PROCEDURE
body.p: Multi-dimensional bit arrays are also supported, for example an 8 by 8 bit grid:

section.title: Multi-bit fields
section.p: The packed field type BIT*N declares an N-bit integer (1 to 8 bits) that can be used on its own, as an array element type, or as an overlay on a byte variable. The overlay form places the field at a bit offset inside the target variable, which is the natural way to model hardware register fields.
section.codeblock:
VAR BYTE config_shadow = 0 VAR BIT*3 speed_field AT config_shadow : 0 -- bits 2:0 VAR BIT*2 mode_field AT config_shadow : 3 -- bits 4:3 VAR BIT*1 enable AT config_shadow : 5 -- bit 5
speed_field = 5 mode_field = 2 enable = TRUE VAR BYTE raw = config_shadow -- 0x35
section.p: BIT*N fields may also be arrayed, for example VAR BIT*3 fields[80] for 80 three-bit values. Widths greater than 8 bits are refused with a diagnostic.

section.title: Bounds and checking
section.p: A constant subscript outside 0 .. N-1 is a compile error (subscript out of range). A runtime index is not range checked, exactly like the other array types, and an open bit-array formal has no compile-time bound inside the callee.
